away.name: Darcy Kuemper
away.news: Kuemper has been far from stellar this season, but through 19 games, he remains the only goalie with a win for the Kings. That said, the 36-year-old veteran goalie is coming off his first shutout of the season, a 29-save performance in a 3-0 win over the Boston Bruins. Before the shutout, Kuemper had allowed eight goals on 38 shots (.789 SV%) during a two-game losing streak (0-2-0). The Kings enter Thursday's game as slight +103 road underdogs against a Toronto Maple Leafs team stuck in a miserable seven-game losing streak (0-7-0).

home.name: Anthony Stolarz
home.news: When the Maple Leafs signed Bobrovsky to a three-year, $7 million AAV contract ($21M total) in the offseason, the hope was that he could solidify their crease and return the team to the postseason. The team has repeatedly given Bobrovsky chances, but he continues to struggle, so Stolarz, who has played well, could be in for a heavier workload. The 32-year-old Stolarz was solid in his most recent outing, saving 22 of 23 shots (.957 SV%), but lost 1-0 to the Edmonton Oilers. The Maple Leafs enter Thursday's game as -112 home favourites against a Los Angeles Kings team that snapped a four-game losing streak with a 3-0 win over the Boston Bruins on Tuesday.

away.name: Joseph Woll
away.news: Despite losing eight of 12 games (4-6-2), Woll has been serviceable on most nights and will return to the crease for the third time in four games. The 28-year-old Woll had a light night in his most recent outing, saving 16 of 19 shots (.842 SV%) in a 4-3 win over the Buffalo Sabres. He has won three straight games, posting a 2.30 GAA and .900 SV%. The Flyers enter Thursday's game against a surging Ottawa Senators team that is 5-0-1 in their past six games.

home.name: Samuel Ersson
home.news: Ersson has not played since Linus Ullmark returned from a lower-body injury earlier this month, but he played well towards the end of his absence and hopes to carry that momentum in Thursday's game. The 27-year-old Errson had a poor start to his tenure with the Senators but has been much better lately, helping his team record at least a point in five straight games (3-0-2) and posting a 1.98 GAA and .925 SV%. The Senators enter Thursday's game as -183 home favourites against Ersson's former team, the Philadelphia Flyers, who are coming off a 4-3 win over the Buffalo Sabres.

away.name: Devon Levi
away.news: For the first time in years, the Oilers are seeing reliable goaltending night in, night out, with Devon Levi leading the way. The 24-year-old Levi was solid in his most recent outing, saving 20 of 22 shots (.909 SV%) in a 5-2 win over the Florida Panthers. Levi has won all four games since returning from a lower-body injury earlier this month, posting an impressive 1.25 GAA and .947 SV%. The Oilers enter Thursday's game as +125 road underdogs against the Tampa Bay Lightning, who are coming off a 5-2 win over the Washington Capitals.

home.name: Andrei Vasilevskiy
home.news: Vasilevskiy led the Lightning onto the ice for warmups.

away.name: Joel Hofer
away.news: Hofer had a rough performance in his most recent outing, allowing four goals on 28 shots (.857 SV%) in a 4-1 loss to the Florida Panthers, but has been terrific on most nights. Before that loss, Hofer posted an impressive 1.82 GAA and .938 SV% over a six-game stretch (4-2-0). The Blues enter Thursday's game as slight -104 road underdogs against the Pittsburgh Penguins, who have not played since Saturday, when they lost 4-1 to the Ottawa Senators.

home.name: Arturs Silovs
home.news: Through 12 games, Silovs has already matched a career high with two shutouts; a misleading stat for mostly unreliable goaltending. The 25-year-old Latvian goalie allowed four goals on 24 shots (.833 SV%) in his most recent outing, a 5-2 loss to the Anaheim Ducks. He has an ugly 4.30 GAA and .840 SV% in his last four games (0-3-1), and has allowed four or more goals in seven of 12 games this season (5-6-1). The Penguins enter Thursday's contest as slight -106 home favourites against the St. Louis Blues, who are coming off a roller-coaster 8-6 win over the Ducks.

away.name: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen
away.news: With Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen and Colten Ellis being unreliable to start the season, the Sabres desperately awaited the return of Alex Lyon (upper body), but he hasn't fared much better in his three games (0-2-1). As such, Luukkonen will return to the crease on Thursday, looking to rebound from his last game on November 11th, when he allowed five goals on 14 shots (.643 SV%) in an 8-3 loss to the Tampa Bay Lightning. The Sabres enter Thursday's contest as +124 road underdogs against the Washington Capitals, losers of three straight (0-3-0).

home.name: Logan Thompson
home.news: Over the past two seasons, Thompson quietly became one of the NHL's most consistent and reliable goalies, coming off consecutive 31-win campaigns. That said, the 29-year-old goalie has been inconsistent at the start of the 2026-27 season. Thompson allowed four goals on 24 shots (.833 SV%) in his most recent outing, a 5-2 loss to the Tampa Bay Lightning, and has allowed four or more goals in six of 14 games this season (7-6-0). The Capitals enter Thursday's game as -133 home favourites against the Buffalo Sabres, who have lost five straight games (0-4-1).

away.name: Jakub Dobes
away.news: After a breakout 2025-26 season that continued with an impressive postseason run, Dobes has struggled early in 2026-27. As a result, the Canadiens have often turned to Jacob Fowler, but they will turn to Dobes in the tail end of a back-to-back on Thursday against the Carolina Hurricanes. Despite his early season struggles, the 25-year-old Dobes has played marginally better lately, posting a 3.04 GAA and .862 SV% in his last three games (2-1-0).

home.name: Pyotr Kochetkov
home.news: Kochetkov led the Hurricanes onto the ice for warmups.

away.name: Cam Talbot
away.news: Jet Greaves has struggled this season, resulting in Talbot playing more in recent weeks, but unfortunately for the Blue Jackets, Talbot's play hasn't been enough. The 39-year-old Talbot was serviceable in his most recent outing, saving 36 of 40 shots (.900 SV%), but he didn't get enough goal support in a 5-1 loss to the New York Islanders. The Blue Jackets have only scored three goals combined in Talbot's past three games (1-2-0). That said, the Blue Jackets enter Thursday's matchup as -158 road favourites against a Chicago Blackhawks team without Connor Bedard (shoulder).

home.name: Spencer Knight
home.news: Knight led the Blackhawks onto the ice for warmups.

away.name: Semyon Varlamov
away.news: Varlamov has been used sparingly this season, but has been serviceable when called upon, especially in recent games. The 38-year-old veteran goalie was solid in his previous outing, saving 26 of 28 shots (.929 SV%) in a 6-2 win over the Anaheim Ducks. In his last five games (2-1-2), Varlamov has a 2.52 GAA and a .904 SV%. The Islanders enter Thursday's game as +104 road underdogs against a Winnipeg Jets team whose six-game winning streak was snapped on Tuesday in a 2-1 loss to the Ottawa Senators.

home.name: Nico Daws
home.news: Daws hasn't played much since being acquired in a trade by the Jets, but he has played well lately in limited action. The 25-year-old German goalie was solid in a relief performance last week, saving 12 of 13 shots (.923 SV%) in a 5-4 shootout win over the Chicago Blackhawks. In four appearances with the Jets (2-1-0), Daws has a 2.32 GAA and a .913 SV%. The Jets enter Thursday's game as slight -104 home underdogs against the New York Islanders, who have outscored opponents 16-5 in their past three games (3-0-0).

away.name: Jesper Wallstedt
away.news: Wallstedt has deservedly been the busiest goalie in the NHL this season, playing 20 of 23 games, posting a tremendous 1.99 GAA and .926 SV% with a 15-2-3 record. The 23-year-old Swedish goalie didn't have to be spectacular in his previous outing, allowing three goals on 28 shots (.893 SV%) in a 7-3 win over the Nashville Predators. With Filip Gustavsson (hip) nearing his season debut, Wallstedt will likely see a slightly lighter workload, but he has proven himself as one of the NHL's best goalies on any given night. Minnesota enters Thursday's game as significant -240 road favourites against the Calgary Flames, who defeated them 2-1 in their only meeting this season.

home.name: Dustin Wolf
home.news: Before being sidelined with a lower-body injury, Devin Cooley owned the crease in Calgary, but he has struggled since returning. Meanwhile, Dustin Wolf seems to have found his game during Cooley's absence. The 25-year-old Wolf was solid in his most recent outing, saving 21 of 23 shots (.913 SV%) in a 5-2 win over the San Jose Sharks. In his last six games (4-1-1), Wolf is boasting an impressive 2.18 GAA and .919 SV%. That said, the Flames enter Thursday's game as sizeable +196 home underdogs against the Central Division-leading Minnesota Wild, who are riding a four-game winning streak.

away.name: Lukas Dostal
away.news: Lukas Dostal has struggled this season and hasn't played much in recent weeks as Head Coach Joel Quenneville has favoured Laurent Brossoit and, more recently, Ville Husso. The 26-year-old Dostal had a forgettable outing in his last start, allowing six goals on 25 shots (.760 SV%) in a 6-2 loss to the New York Islanders. He has allowed three or more goals in seven straight starts (2-4-1). The Ducks enter Thursday's game as slight +111 road underdogs against an injury-depleted Colorado Avalanche team that lost 4-1 last night to the Utah Mammoth.

away.name: Leevi Merilainen
away.news: The Canucks have struggled regardless of who is tending the twine this season, but Merilainen has been their most reliable option, and he will return to the crease on Thursday. The 24-year-old Finnish goalie was solid in his most recent outing, saving 34 of 37 shots (.919 SV%) in a rare 6-3 win over the Vegas Golden Knights. The win snapped Merilainen's six-game losing streak (0-6-0). The Canucks enter Thursday's outing as +145 road underdogs against the Seattle Kraken, who have been outscored 13-5 during a three-game losing streak (0-3-0).

home.name: Philipp Grubauer
home.news: Grubauer played well in relief of Joey Daccord last week, saving 22 of 23 shots (.957 SV%) in a 5-1 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes. That said, the 34-year-old Grubauer has had an inconsistent season, as he has throughout his tenure with the Seattle Kraken. He has allowed three or more goals in his last six starts (3-2-1). Still, Seattle enters Thursday's game as -165 home favourites against a league-worst Vancouver Canucks team that has won two straight games.

away.name: Jake Oettinger
away.news: Oettinger leads the NHL with four shutouts, suggesting he has been one of the NHL's best goalies, but in reality, he has been fairly inconsistent. The 27-year-old American goalie was serviceable in his most recent game, saving 24 of 27 shots (.889 SV%) in a 4-3 win over the Vegas Golden Knights, but it was the eighth time in 16 games (11-4-1) that he has posted a sub-.900 SV%. The Stars enter Thursday's rematch against the Golden Knights as +109 road underdogs.

home.name: Adin Hill
home.news: The Golden Knights have had an even goalie rotation in recent weeks, but will turn to Hill for consecutive games on Thursday in a rematch against the Dallas Stars, despite allowing four goals on 22 shots (.818 SV%) against them in a 4-3 loss on Tuesday. That said, the 30-year-old Hill was playing well before Tuesday's loss, posting a 1.98 GAA and .931 SV% in his previous five games (3-1-1). The Golden Knights enter Thursday's game as -121 home favourites against the Stars, who are 6-1-1 in their last eight games.
